name: Srclight

hlido_opinion.headline: Local-first code-indexing MCP server for AI agents — hybrid FTS5 + tree-sitter + embeddings in a single SQLite file, fully offline, 25 tools.
hlido_opinion.body: Srclight targets a real and growing pain: coding agents burn context and latency making dozens of grep/glob calls to understand a repo, and Srclight offers to replace that with a precise, structured index they can query over MCP. The engineering choices on the public surface are tasteful and coherent — a single SQLite file per repo (no external database, no Docker, no cloud), tree-sitter for precise symbol extraction plus call graphs, and a hybrid search that fuses FTS5 keyword matching with semantic embeddings via reciprocal rank fusion. The privacy posture is a genuine differentiator: embeddings run locally through Ollama, so code never leaves the machine, and it explicitly supports air-gapped and private repos. Twenty-five MCP tools, a one-line pip install, multi-repo workspaces and an optional GPU-accelerated vector cache round out a surprisingly complete story for a young project. The caveats are the caveats of youth and of a public-surface read: the star count is small (early adoption), the performance claims (sub-3ms semantic queries, 60-second setup) are documented rather than independently benchmarked here, and the local-embeddings path adds an Ollama dependency and hardware expectations that the landing page soft-pedals. For agent builders who want retrieval that stays on their own hardware, it is a well-conceived, honestly-scoped tool worth watching.

tier_rationale: STEADY (72), medium confidence. It clears the STEADY bar on a clear, well-argued value proposition (structured index over MCP to cut agent grep/glob overhead), a privacy-first local/offline architecture that is a real differentiator, and a genuinely complete feature surface for its age (25 tools, hybrid search, multi-repo, MIT, PyPI). Kept out of the higher band because adoption is still early (small star count) and the notable performance claims are documented but not independently verified in this public-surface review.
what_it_does_well: Replaces dozens of agent grep/glob calls with a precise, structured, queryable index over MCP
Fully local and offline: local embeddings via Ollama, so code never leaves the machine (air-gapped/private-repo friendly)
Minimal footprint — a single SQLite file per repo, no external DB, Docker or cloud services
Hybrid retrieval done right: FTS5 keyword + semantic embeddings fused via reciprocal rank fusion, plus tree-sitter symbol/call-graph extraction
Complete surface for a young project: 25 MCP tools, one-line pip install, multi-repo workspaces, MIT license on PyPI
what_it_fails_at: Early adoption — small GitHub star count and limited independent track record
Headline performance claims (sub-3ms semantic queries, 60-second setup) are documented, not independently benchmarked here
Local-embeddings path adds an Ollama dependency and real hardware expectations the landing page underplays
Public surface is a single landing page; depth of the 25 tools is described more than demonstrated
best_for: Agent builders who want code retrieval that stays entirely on their own hardware
Private-repo, air-gapped or compliance-sensitive teams that can't send code to a cloud indexer
Claude Code / Cursor / Windsurf users wanting to cut token spend on repository exploration
not_recommended_for: Teams that prefer a fully managed, hosted code-intelligence service with no local setup
Users unwilling to run Ollama / provision local embedding compute
Anyone needing a proven, large-scale production track record today

compared_to.verdict_diff: Sourcegraph Cody is a mature, largely hosted code-intelligence platform; Srclight is a young, local-first indexing layer exposed purely over MCP. Choose Cody for enterprise-scale hosted code search; choose Srclight when the requirement is that nothing leaves the machine and the consumer is an agent, not a human IDE.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Direct MCP server (srclight serve) with 25 tools, connectable from Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf or any MCP client. Also a CLI for indexing. Purpose-built to be driven by agents for code retrieval — highly composable.
